correctness.rationale: The complete eight-bigram substitution closure constructs all length-eight factors at both parity phases; it gives disjoint sets of sizes 24 and 32, independently replayed from certificate.json. Any circular all-rotations word of length >=9 has alternating uniquely determined eight-window phases around the entire circle, hence even length. The 4-to-2 binary coding tau∘sigma is a bijection on aligned two-bit blocks, so even-length qualifying binary conjugacy classes inject into four-letter qualifying classes at half length. The four-letter fixed point alternates letter types {a,d}/{b,c}, forcing any qualifying length >=2 to be even and admitting a second injective sigma desubstitution. Thus outside powers of two no long classes exist and at each large power at most four survive. The four explicit words tau(sigma^k(x)) have all rotations witnessed across one of two legal neighboring bigrams by equal first/last halves; the eight-window parity and repeated even desubstitution distinguish their four cyclic classes. Exact short classes n=1..8 are reconstructed from exhaustive supertile factors. The fresh verifier checks every length to 128 and power witnesses to 512 but is not used as an infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new theorem is not a relabeling of the 1993 injection lemma or a generic consequence of Bell–Shallit automaticity. Those premises alone do not assert or enumerate the conjugacy classes; the proof establishes cyclic alternation, descent to a one-letter constraint, and four dyadic witnesses. Its value is the exact natural invariant, not novelty of an already known coding property.

value.rationale: Lie complexity was introduced specifically to quantify conjugacy classes all of whose cyclic representatives are factors. The canonical Rudin–Shapiro 2-automatic sequence is a natural omitted test case in the motivating explicit examples. The theorem supplies the complete all-length formula, a sharp sparse dyadic-support classification, and the actual four surviving classes at every large dyadic length. The proof explains the phenomenon structurally by two injective circular desubstitutions; it is not a routine finite table, a rename of the 1993 phase lemma, or a marginal bound improvement.
